orders.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND 
AT NAINITAL
Anticipatory Bail Application No. 692 of 2025
Reena Bisht. …….Applicant.
Versus
State of Uttarakhand. ….…Respondent. 
Present:
Mr. Aditya Singh, learned counsel for the applicant.
Mr. G.S. Sandhu, learned Addl. Advocate General with Mr. Pradeep Lohani, learned Brief Holder for 
the State.
Mr. Neeraj Pandey, learned counsel for the complainant.
Hon’ble Mr. Justice Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. The present applicant is praying for anticipatory bail in 
relation to FIR dated 21.05.2025 bearing FIR No. 0049 of 2025, 
Police Station – Shyampur, District – Haridwar lodged by one
Smt. Geetanjali Giri, wife of Mahant Rohit Giri, implicating 
present applicant along with her husband Mahant Rohit Giri, 
Meena Chauhan, Sameer, Tej Prakhash Bisht, Raj Kumar Mishra, 
Ritik, Vijay Mohan Panwar, Sonu and Sonu Kashyap @ Mogli for 
the offences punishable under Section 109 (1), 303 (1), 308 (2), 308 
(3), read with Section 61 (2) (b) of BNS, 2023. During ongoing 
investigation, Section 308 (3) of BNS, 2023 is converted to Section 
308 (7) of BNS, 2023.
2. Brief facts of the case are that complainant Smt. Geetanjali 
Giri married with Mahant Rohit Giri on 07.03.2006, from which 
one male child was born, who is aged about 19 years old as on 
date. Due to some matrimonial dispute in between both of them, 
a petition under Section 13 B of the Hindu Marriage Act was filed
on 07.03.2022 seeking divorce by way of mutual consent wherein 
it is contended that both of them are living separately since 
21.05.2018. In this petition, first motion was completed but 
second motion was failed. Thereafter, on 30.09.2023, Mahant  2
Rohit Giri filed another divorce petition under Section 13 (1) (i-b) 
of the Hindu Marriage Act seeking divorce on the ground of 
desertion. In paragraph 4 and 5 of the petition, date of desertion 
is mentioned as 21.05.2018 and this is the same date, which was 
mentioned in the petition filed Section 13 B of the Hindu 
Marriage Act. 
3. It is argued by the learned counsel for the applicant Mr. 
Aditya Singh that on 22.08.2024 in the aforesaid divorce petition 
the concerned court ordered to proceed ex parte and for recalling 
the order of ex parte, the complainant – Smt. Geetanjali filed an 
application along with affidavit under Order 9 Rule 7 read with 
Section 151 CPC on 18.01.2025. 
4. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that in both the 
petitions filed under Section 13 B and under Section 13 (1) (i-b) of 
the Hindu Marriage Act, address of the complainant is the same
and in both the divorce petitions the date of desertion is same i.e. 
21.05.2018 and the address of the complainant and Mahant Rohit 
Giri are also different which itself reveals that both of them are 
living separately since 21.05.2018. 
5. Learned counsel for the applicant further argued that so far 
as present applicant is concerned she is in live-in-relation with 
Mahant Rohit Giri for the last more than one year and from this 
living relation, one female child was born on 14.01.2025 and both 
of them the applicant and Mahant Rohit Giri are residing together 
in the same house along with minor child. 
6. Mr. Aditya Singh, learned counsel for the applicant, 
submits that Mahant Rohit Giri of Maa Chandi Devi Temple with 
whom the applicant was in live in relation was arrested by 
Punjab Police from Neel Parvat, Haridwar where the temple is  3
located, in a molestation case filed by a woman from Ludhiyana 
(Punjab) in which a non bailable warrant was issued. 
7. Learned counsel for the applicant further submits that after 
seven days of arrest of Mahant Rohit Giri on 21.05.2025 Smt. 
Geetanajali lodged a first information report implicating 
applicant and Mahant Rohit Giri with others raising various 
allegations and one of the allegation is that her husband Mahant 
Giri informed that the applicant Reena Bisht made a video of 
physical relationship and he is praying money otherwise, the 
video would be made viral. It is further alleged that on hearing 
the arrest of Mahant Rohit Giri, complainant reached at the house 
of Mahant Rohit Giri and during this period, the applicant tried 
to run over her son by her car. Learned counsel further argued 
that all the allegations, as alleged in the FIR, are completely false, 
baseless and after thought which is evident from the fact that 
though Mahant Rohit Giri was arrested on 14.05.2025 but in the 
FIR, Mahant Rohit Giri is also implicated for the alleged incident 
of 14.05.2025 and not only this after 7 days of the alleged incident 
FIR was lodged. He further submits that the allegation, as alleged 
in the FIR, against the applicant is highly improbable, since at 
that time, applicant was having 4 month old daughter and no 
prudent person can presume that such an incident can be caused 
by the present applicant. 
8. On the other side, Mr. Neeraj Pandey, who put his 
appearance on behalf of the complainant submits that since 
Mahant Rohit Giri resigned on 13.05.2025, one day prior to his 
arrest wherein he proposed to appoint his son to perform the 
duties of Mahant, consequently, after the arrest of Mahant Rohit 
Giri, his son namely Shri Bhawani Nand Giri, who is 19 years old 
resume the charge of Mahant. 4
9. Mr. Neeraj Pandey, learned counsel for the complainant 
further argued that all the arguments advanced by Mr. Aditya 
Singh are thoroughly misconceived. Even the date of desertion as 
mentioned in the petition are not admitted and in fact, in the 
divorce petition written statements was filed wherein 
complainant has categorically stated that she is living separately 
from Mahant Rohit Giri since 22.05.2023 and this is absolutely 
incorrect to say that she is living separately since 21.05.2018. 
Apart from this, he further submits that living relation of the 
present applicant with Mahant Rohit Giri is not permissible in 
view of Section 380 (2) of the UCC Act, 2024. 
10. Apart from this, Mr. Neeraj Pandey, learned counsel for the 
complainant, submits that present applicant had removed the 
CCTV camera installed in the premises of temple.
11. On this, Mr. Aditya Singh, learned counsel for the 
applicant, has seriously object by submitting that since the 
applicant was having 4 month old daughter and Mahant Rohit 
Giri was arrested on 14.05.2025, therefore, it is highly improbable 
for her to remove the CCTV camera and it’s footage and 
furthermore, the allegations, as alleged in the FIR, are completely 
baseless, which is evident from the fact that in reference of 
incident of 14.05.2025, the FIR has been lodged after 7 days. He 
further submits that no such resignation as per his information 
was given by Mahant Rohit Giri and it is manufactured one. 
12. Yesterday, when the matter was listed, Mr. Aditya Singh, 
learned counsel for the applicant pointed out that on the date of 
arrest of Mahant Rohit Giri, on the charge of molestation by 
Punjab police the complainant entered in the premises of temple 
by projecting herself as a Trustee of the Trust and she made an 
attempt to take over the management of the temple. 5
13. This Court took very serious note of serious charge of 
molestation by a woman against Mahant Rohit Giri of the Mahant 
of Maa Chandi Devi Temple, which is one of the most ancient 
temple in the northern India, which is said to have been founded 
in 8th Century by Adi Guru Shankaracharya, one of the top priest 
of the Hindu Religion, which obviously hurt the sentiments of 
lakh of devotees. This Court instruct to Mr. G.S. Sandhu, Addl. 
Advocate General to ask the District Magistrate and SSP, 
Haridwar to join the proceedings through V.C. and in compliance 
thereof, both the officers joined the proceedings through V.C. and 
this Court direct them to monitor the entire situation and to 
maintain law and order in the entire premises of temple and get 
instructions from the Ministry of Tourism and Religious Affairs
what preventive measure can be taken in the premises of temple 
since thousands of devotees visits everyday in the temple for 
Darshan as well as to perform pooja. 
14. Today, District Magistrate as well as SSP, Haridwar joined 
the proceedings through V.C. and apprise this Court that there is 
a Committee called as Badrinath Kedarnath Temple Committee
(in short BKTC) and this Committee is managing affairs of
various temples in the State including Badrinath and Kedarnath 
temples. 
15. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and taking into 
consideration the allegation, as alleged in the FIR, prima facie, 
this Court is of the view that the trustees of the temple are 
creating noxious atmosphere in the temple and there is complete 
mismanagement in the trust and it cannot be ruled out that there 
may be misappropriation of donation. Apart from this since there 
are serious allegations of molestation against Mahant Rohit Giri
of which this Court already take serious note of it. Apart from  6
this, there are also serious allegations, as alleged in the FIR, which 
requires thorough investigation for which SSP Haridwar is 
directed to depute a senior officer not below the rank of Dy. S.P. 
to investigate the matter and inquire about the conduct of the 
applicant as well as of the complainant and also against the 
persons against whom FIR has been lodged. SSP, Haridwar is 
also directed to monitor the entire investigation and apprise this 
Court about the status of investigation on the next date. 
16. Apart from this, taking into consideration that Maa Chandi 
Devi Temple is an ancient temple of northern India and 
thousands of devotees visit everyday for pooja and Darshan in 
the temple, therefore, till the investigation is completed, this 
Court is primarily of the view that some preventive measures 
requires to be taken.
17. Mr. Ravi Babulkar, learned counsel for the Badrinath 
Kedarnath Temple Committee (in short BKTC) on instructions, 
submits that there is Badrinath Kedarnath Temple Committee 
Act, 1939 and under this Act, the Committee controls the affairs 
of various temples and as such, Badrinath Kedarnath Temple 
Committee (in short BKTC) can supervise the affairs of the 
existing Managing Trust of the Maa Chandi Devi Temple.
18. In such view of the matter, till the investigation is 
completed, the existing Trust shall continue but the existing Trust 
will act under the direct control and supervision of Badrinath 
Kedarnath Temple Committee (in short BKTC) and for that 
purpose, the District Administration is directed to provide full 
assistance to the Badrinath Kedarnath Temple Committee(in 
short BKTC). Apart from this Badrinath Kedarnath Temple 
Committee (in short BKTC) is directed to appoint “Receiver” 
immediately. Furthermore, since the investigation is going on in  7
such an eventuality, applicant and complainant are restrained 
from interfering in day to day affairs of the Managing Trust of 
Maa Chandi Devi Temple. 
19. Since applicant is praying for anticipatory bail, therefore, 
keeping in view the fact that since applicant is having four month 
old daughter, this Court is of the view that till the investigation is 
going on, applicant deserves for interim protection. In such an 
eventuality, let the investigation may go on, but in the event of 
arrest of the applicant – Reena Bisht, she shall be released on 
interim bail on executing a personal bond of Rs. 30,000/- and two 
reliable sureties, of the like amount, to the satisfaction of the 
Investigating Officer/ Arresting Officer, subject to the following 
conditions:
(i) Applicant as well as complainant shall cooperate 
with the investigating agency and make themselves
available for interrogation by the concerned 
Investigating Officer as and when required; 
(ii) Applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any 
inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted 
with the facts of this case and; 
(iii) Applicant shall not leave the country without 
previous permission of this Court. 
(iv) SSP, Haridwar is also directed to monitor the 
investigation as well as maintain law and order in the 
entire premises of Maa Chandi Devi Temple and he 
shall ensure that no one put any harm to any devotee, 
who visits the temple for pooja. 8
(v) District Administration is directed to give full 
assistance to officials of the Badrinath Kedarnath 
Temple Committee (in short BKTC). 
20. Respondents may file counter affidavit within four weeks. 
Two weeks, thereafter, is granted to the applicant to file rejoinder 
affidavit.
21. List on 13.08.2025.
 (Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)
 25.06.2025
SKS

Hon'ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Mr. Aakash Sanyal, learned counsel 
holding the brief of Mr. Aditya Singh, 
learned counsel for the petitioner.
2. Mr. Tumul Nainwal, learned A.G.A. 
for the State.
3. Mr. U.K. Uniyal, learned Senior 
Advocate (through V.C.) assisted by Mr. 
Pragya Prakash Upadhyay, learned 
counsel for the complainant-Geetanjali.
4. Mr. Vipul Sharma, learned counsel 
with Mr. Ravi Babulkar, learned counsel 
BKTC.
5. All these matters are listed today. 
The Hon’ble Supreme Court by judgment 
and order dated 25.06.2025, remand
this matter in order to expedite the same 
by directing the Collector, Haridwar to 
conduct a personal inquiry with regard to 
the management of the Math, after 
hearing all the parties. The Collector, 
Haridwar was also directed that he shall 
focus on the best interest of the Math 
and its devotees and submit a report to 
the High Court. 6. In compliance to the Hon’ble Apex 
Court’s directions the Collector, Haridwar 
placed its report. The Hon’ble Apex Court 
also directed the BKTC to give up-to￾date report to the High Court and keep 
on submitting periodic updated report.
7. Put up this matter on 26.02.2026. 
By that time, BKTC also place before this 
Court updated report as per the direction 
of the Hon’ble Apex Court.
8. Mr. Tumul Nainwal, learned A.G.A. 
for the State informed this Court that in 
WPCRL NO. 1679 of 2025, the petitioner, 
namely, Mahant Rohit Giri is not 
cooperating with the investigation, 
though, Mahant Rohit Giri was given 
protection by the Coordinate Bench 
subject to this condition that he will 
cooperate with the investigation.
9. Learned counsel for Mahant Rohit 
Giri make a statement that he will join 
the investigation today itself and also in 
future date.
10. Earlier, investigation is being 
carried out in FIR No. 49 of 2025 and Mr. 
Tumul Nainwal, learned A.G.A. apprise 
this Court that in this FIR charge sheet 
has been filed and eight persons have 
been exonerated and two persons have 
been charge sheeted. So far as other two 
FIRs, i.e. FIR No. 308 of 2025 and FIR 
No. 139 of 2025 are concerned, in FIR 
No. 318 of 2025, Mr. Tumul Nainwal 
already apprise to this Court that 
Mahant Rohit Giri is not cooperating with 
the investigation, though, now statement 
has been given by learned counsel that 
Mahant Rohit Giri shall join the 
investigation today itself and also on 
future date. So far as another FIR No. 
1319 of 2025 is concerned, Mr. Tumul 
Nainwal, learned A.G.A. seeks time to  get instructions so that on the next date 
he shall apprise to this Court about 
status of investigation in the FIR No. 
1319 of 2025
11. Interim orders, if any, in all these 
matters are extended till the next date of 
listing.
12. Personal appearance of the Collector 
is exempted.
(Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)

Hon’ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J. 
1. None appears for the applicant.
2. Mr. Sandeep Sharma, learned A.G.A. for the 
State.
3. In compliance to the previous order the Collector 
as well as BKTC submitted its report and the same are 
opened, court perused the same. Let both the report be 
treated part of the record.
4. The Collector’s report is marked as ‘report-A’ 
and the report of the BKTC is marked as ‘report-B’. 
From the Collector’s report it reveals that the 
Collector’s report is not as per the direction of the 
Hon’ble Apex Court dated 19.08.2025, whereby, the 
Collector was directed to focus on the best interest for 
the math and its devotees. It appears from the report of 
the Collector that the Collector only submitted the 
report with regard to the present situation of temple 
and its premises including the facilities but what would 
be the best in the interest of math and its devotees this 
is completely missing, therefore, the Collector is 
directed to submit a report strictly as per the direction 
of the Hon’ble Apex Court focusing on the interest for 
the math and its devotees.
5. Put up this matter on 27.03.2026.
 
 (Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)

Reena Bisht --Applicant
 Versus
State Of Uttarakhand --Respondent
Hon'ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
Mr. Raghav Singhal, learned counsel 
holding brief of Mr. Aditya Singh, learned 
counsel for the applicant. 
2. Mr. G.S. Sandhu, learned Additional 
Advocate General assisted by Mr. Deepak 
Bhardwaj, learned Brief Holder for the State. 
3. Mr. Neeraj Garg and Mr. M.C. Pant, 
learned counsel for the interveners of IA No.02 of 
2025 and IA No.05 of 2026. 
4. Mr. B.S. Adhikari, learned counsel for the 
informant/complainant. 
5. However, while dictating the judgment for 
certain issues matter is posted today for further 
argument. 
6. When this anticipatory bail application 
came up before this Court on 25.06.2026, this 
Court take very serious note of the serious 
charges of molestation against the Mahant Rohit 
Giri, Mahant of math Chandi Devi temple and for 
an interim measure till the investigation is 
completed, the existing trust was permitted to 
continue under the direct control and supervision 
of the Badrinath Kedarnath Temple Committee 
(in short BKTC), a statutory body, governed 
under the 1939 Act with the further direction that  District Administration shall provide full 
assistance to the said Committee and for an 
interim measure, the applicant was granted 
interim protection by granting interim bail 
subject to certain conditions. 
7. Aforesaid order was assailed before the 
Apex Court by the present Trustee/Mahant 
Bhawani Nandan Giri in Special Leave to Appeal 
(Criminal) No.11285 of 2025 and the Hon’ble 
Supreme Court on 19.08.2025 remand the matter 
without disturbing the order dated 25.06.2025 
with the direction to decide the issue of 
permanent management of the Trust by focusing 
on the best interest of the “math” and its 
“devotees”. The Collector was also directed to 
submit a report. The BKTC was also directed to 
submit up to date report to the High Court.
8. While remanding the matter, the Hon’ble 
Supreme Court also requested to the High Court 
to implead the persons, who may not be the 
party before the High Court and have been heard 
and also requested to take up the matter on 
priority and decide the issue, so that an 
arrangement/regular arrangement is put into 
place rather than an ad-hoc arrangement. Thus 
the mandate of the remand order of the Supreme 
Court was to decide the issue for 
permanent/regular arrangement on the best 
interest of the “math and its devotees”.
9. After remand some of the interveners 
moved applications i.e. IA No.02 of 2025 and IA 
No.05 of 2026 and both the applications were 
allowed 23.04.2026. After remand IA No.03 of 
2026 has been moved on behalf of the informant￾Mrs. Geetanjali Giri by annexing certain previous 
orders of this Court as well as one of the order of 
the Supreme Court.  10. Subsequently, one more IA No.04 of 2026 
has been moved by the informant annexing the 
order dated 03.01.2026 passed in WPPIL No.02 of 
2011 and the order of Hon’ble Supreme Court 
dated 16.01.2017, wherein the order of High 
Court dated 30.01.2012 was assailed in order to 
demonstrate that infact the issue with regard to 
the management of the Trust has already attains 
finality pursuant to the judgment dated 
03.01.2012 passed in WPPIL No.02 of 2011. 
11. Mr. Neeraj Garg and Mr. M.C. Pant, 
learned counsel, who appears for the interveners 
submits that the issue in hand is only confined to 
decide the mandate of the order of remand 
passed by the Hon’ble Supreme Court, therefore, 
the previous orders, passed in different 
proceedings, which has been brought on record 
by way of IA No.03 of 2026 on behalf of the 
informant have no relevance. Order of this Court 
dated 25.06.2025 has not been disturbed by the 
Hon’ble Supreme Court. They argued that the 
mandate, as given by the Apex Court under it’s 
remand order is in a larger public interest, since 
the sentiments of lakhs of devotees are attached 
with the temple in question.
11. Learned counsel for the applicant also 
supports that submission of learned counsel for 
the interveners Mr. Neeraj Garg and Mr. B.S. 
Adhikari.
12. In such an eventuality, on the submission, 
as advanced by Mr. Neeraj Garg and Mr. B.S. 
Adhikari, learned counsel for the interveners and 
learned counsel for the applicant, let they may 
file their objections to the IA No.03 of 2026 
moved on behalf of the interveners within two 
weeks. 
13. List this matter on 30.07.2026 on top of the 
board.  14. Registry is directed to supply the copy of 
IA No.03 of 2026 to Mr. Neeraj Garg and Mr. 
M.C. Pant, learned counsel for the interveners as 
well as to learned Government Advocate 
forthwith. 
(Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)
 07.07.2026

Hon’ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
Mr. Aditya Singh, learned counsel for the 
applicant.
2. Mr. Tumul K Nainwal, learned AGA, for the 
State of Uttarakhand.
3. Mr. Neeraj Garg and Mr. M.C. Pant, learned 
counsel for the interveners of IA No.02 of 2025 and IA 
No.05 of 2026.
4. Mr. B.S. Adhikari, learned counsel for the 
informant/complainant. 
5. Mr. Ravi Babulkar, learned counsel for the 
BKTC.
6. Mr. B.D. Pandey, learned counsel for the IA 
No.06 of 2026.
7. IA No.03 of 2026, is moved on behalf of the 
complainant – Ms. Geetanjali Giri, wherein, certain 
orders of this Court in the previous litigations are 
enclosed alongwith and the case details uploaded 
from the High Court website of different litigations as 
well as one of the orders of the Hon’ble Apex Court 
dated 04.12.2025, and one order passed in AO No.208 
of 2016, which is in different context, with the request 
that these orders be taken on record. This application 
admittedly has been moved after remanding the 
matter by the Hon’ble Apex Court.
8. Thereafter, IA No.05 of 2026, is moved by one 
of the interveners Mr. Ramesh Chandra Lakhera, 
which was allowed, wherein, he has pointed out the 
mismanagement in the Trust as well as 
misappropriate of donations and offerings, and 
stopping this intervener to perform the “Puja”. 
9. In IA No.03 of 2026, Mr. Neeraj Garg, filed 
objections on behalf of Mahant Ashish Puri, who 
earlier filed an impleadment application i.e. IA No.02 
of 2025, which was already allowed on 23.04.2026.
10. Mr. B.D. Pandey, learned counsel also filed IA  No.06 of 2026, on behalf of one Mahant Ravi Giri S/o 
Late Mahant Dinesh Giri, to be impleaded as 
party/respondent. In this IA, he has enclosed an order 
of National Green Tribunal dated 24.08.2018, whereby 
the NGT constitute a Committee headed by Justice Mr. 
U.C. Dhyani, former Judge of this Court, giving a task 
which is reflected from paragraph 7, and also enclosed 
subsequent order of the National Green Tribunal. On 
perusal of these orders, it reveals that the National 
Green Tribunal take serious note of the rampant 
encroachment over the Forest land, then giving on 
rent, by the Trust. Consequently, on 18.03.2020, the 
National Green Tribunal observed in the order, which 
reads as under:-
“The Executive and Forest authorities shall, 
however, continue to make all efforts to bring 
pending cases to their logical conclusion and 
ensure that no new encroachment takes place.”
11. The Committee so constituted by the National 
Green Tribunal submitted its report before the 
National Green Tribunal on 29.11.2019, and the extract 
of the report is also reflected from the order of the 
National Green Tribunal dated 18.03.2020, which 
reads as under:-
“4. Summary of achievements mentioned in the 
report is as follows:-
"a. The shops and structures outside the pillars of 
the lease area of Dakshin Kali temple have been 
demolished.
b. Eviction order has been issued against the 
Respondent in Chandikeshwar Mahadev and Ved 
Karmkand 
c. Some shops and other structures which were 
operating from land outside the lease area of 
Upper Chandi Devi temple have been demolished. 
Additional 46 illegal structures have been 
identified and notices have been served to them.
d. A Forest Offence has been lodged before the 
court of Divisional Forest Officer and is presently 
under proceedings under Section-61A of Indian 
Forest Act, 1927 (State Amendment) in the 
matter of Anjani Mata Temple.
e. A Forest Offence has been lodged before the  court of Divisional Forest Officer and is presently 
under proceedings under Section-61A of 
Indian Forest Act 1927 (State Amendment) in the 
matter of Gaurishankar temple. Presently, car 
parking in the area has been stopped and trees 
have been planted in its place.
f. Another parking near Gaurishankar temple has 
been stopped by the DFO. This land is under 
transfer to NHAI towards broadening of the 
National Highway-74, for which forest clearance 
has been granted.
g. Show cause notice has been issued to the 
Respondent as to why the encroachments be not 
removed from forest land in the matter of 
Nileshwar Mahadev temple.
h. The liquor shop along the highway, running on 
Forest land and transferred to Irrigation 
department in the past, has been demolished and 
unauthorized occupants evicted.
i. In the matter of Sidhbali ashram, DFO has 
passed eviction order against the encroachers. The 
Respondents have removed the additional 
structures.
j. DFO has issued eviction orders in the matter of 
Sidhsot ashram.
k. In-principle approval under the Forest 
Conservation Act, 1980 has been obtained on 
5.2.2011 and the conditions have been complied 
with in the matter of Police Wireless building.
l. Haridwar Roorkee Development Authority has 
sent notices to 14 illegal constructions within 100 
m of River Ganga and demolition order has been 
passed in two cases, one unauthorized 
construction has been sealed, seven cases were 
found beyond 200 m of river Ganga as per report 
of the Irrigation department and the remaining 
four are pending decision. No new encroachment 
has been reported.
m. Two shops at Chandi Devi ropeway station, 4 
shops near Ropeway parking area and 1 shop at 
starting point of Chandi Devi trek path, were 
forcefully evicted and demolished as per law. In 
addition, 3 shops adjacent to Mahant niwas, 3 
shops on Anjani mandir path and all shops of 
temporary nature along Chandi devi temple path 
have been removed.
n. All unauthorized constructions from Singh 
Dwar to Buddhi Mata Mandir and Laksar road 
and all such constructions from Pul Jatwara to  Mansa Devi temple have been demolished in 
Haridwar town.
o. The Nodal Officer, Forest Conservation has 
directed the Chief Medical Officer, Tehri Garhwal 
to vacate the expired lease of Brahmpuri Kusht 
colony at the earliest.
p. Eviction order has been passed against 261 
encroachers in the case of Bengali basti, 
Mayakund, Rishikesh, with respect to OA 
311/2019 Markandey Ram vs State of 
Uttarakhand. Out of 261 persons, SO persons 
have vacated the premises on their own. The 
remaining encroachments have been completely 
evicted and all the structures have been 
completely demolished.
It is being ensured that no fresh encroachments or 
constructions are taking place anywhere within 
100 m from River Ganga and in the adjacent 
forest areas."
12. IA No.07 of 2026, has been moved on behalf of 
the intervener Mr. Ramesh Chandra Lakhera, in a 
reference to the response to IA No.03 of 2026, filed by 
the complainant, wherein, in paragraph 8, it is stated 
that the applicant of IA No.03 of 2026 – Ms. Geetanjali 
Giri, placed on record the orders of previous 
litigations for oblique purposes, and motivating 
apprehension of bias and application is misconceived 
and is abuse of process of law. In paragraph 24, it is 
stated that the existing Management/Trustees are 
functioning on the basis of the frivolous and fabricated 
Supplementary Trust Deed dated 27.05.2025, executed 
in office of Sub-Registrar, Rishikesh, on the alleged 
resignation of Mahant Rohit Giri, though Mahant 
Rohit Giri, denied about his resignation and pursuant 
to the directions of the ACJM, Haridwar, an FIR 
No.139 of 2025, has also been registered at P.S. 
Shyampur, against the applicant of IA No.03 of 2026 –
Geetanjali Giri and her son Sri Bhawani Nandan Giri, 
brother-in-law Sri Akash Kusum Bachheti and sister￾in-law Ms. Pushpanjali Gaur, and others. In this IA, it 
is prayed that IA No.03 of 2026, be rejected with costs. 
13. Mr. Neeraj Garg, Mr. M.C.Pant as well as Mr. 
B.D. Pandey, learned counsels argued that by moving 
IA No.03 of 2026, the complainant is diverting the  issue of remand order of Hon’ble Apex Court and it is 
deliberate with some vested interest. 
14. Let the State may also get the status of 
investigation of that FIR lodged by Mahant Rohit Giri.
15. In the objections of Mahant Ashish Puri, on IA 
No.03 of 2026, a suggestion has been given to appoint 
any retired Judge of Hon’ble Apex Court/retired 
Chief Justice/retired Judge of High Court, to be act as 
Chief Administrator, and sought specific directions to 
the Director General of Police and the Chief Secretary
of the State to ensure removal of bouncers, who are 
engaged by the applicant of IA No.03 of 2026, within 
temple premises. 
16. Since now the objections has been filed in IA 
No.03 of 2026, an application moved by Ms. Geetanjali 
Giri and the Ms. Geetanjali Giri, is also one of the 
party respondents, herein, who is complainant and is 
being represented by Mr. B.S. Adhikari, who prays for 
and is granted two weeks’ time to file response. Mr. 
B.S. Adhikari, learned counsel shall also file response 
to the suggestion as given by Mr. Neeraj Garg, learned 
counsel for appointment of retired Judge of Hon’ble 
Apex Court/retired Chief Justice/retired Judge of 
High Court, to be act as Chief Administrator.
17. Mr. Aditya Singh, learned counsel, accepted the 
suggestion for appointment of retired Hon’ble Judge 
to be act as Chief Administrator, however, Mr. B.S. 
Adhikari, learned counsel has some reservation for 
appointment of Hon’ble Retired Judge as Chief 
Administrator. 
18. At this juncture, let the response may be filed 
within two weeks.
19. Mr. B.S. Adhikari, learned counsel make a 
statement, on instructions, that no bouncers have been 
deputed in the temple premises.
20. At this juncture, it is also relevant to mention, 
as pointed by the learned counsel for the parties, that 
Mr. Bhawani Nandan Giri, approached to the Hon’ble 
Apex Court, in which the matter was remanded, but 
he is not the party respondent, herein, therefore, and 
the Hon’ble Apex Court while remanding the matter 
gives an opportunity to all of them to raise objections 
in this pending proceedings and as such he is 
permitted to be impleaded as one of the respondent  during the course of the day. 
21. Mr. B.S. Adhikari, learned counsel shall disclose 
about the expenditure and receiving of its offerings 
and donations of last ten years. 
22. Mr. Aditya Singh, learned for the applicant 
prays for and is granted time to file supplementary 
affidavit brining on record certain relevant documents.
23. Mr. Ravi Babulkar, learned counsel shall also 
file the affidavit with regard to the details of receipts 
of offerings and donations since the date when the 
BKTC, is looking after the affairs of the Trust.
24. The concerned District Magistrate and the SSP, 
shall also file their affidavits with regard to the details 
of the receipts of offerings and the donations since the 
date when the earlier Division Bench passed the order 
on 03.01.2012.
25. List this matter on 31.08.2026, under the 
heading of “Remand Matter by Hon’ble Apex Court”.
26. Registry is directed to show the name of Mr. 
Ravi Babulkar, as learned counsel for the BKTC in the 
cause list.
 (Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)
